items.line: Unusual Whales says Bloomington, Indiana, has banned artificial superintelligence, with a 7-0 council vote, fines for violators, and a repeal bar of more than 95 percent of registered voters. A local paper confirms the vote but describes the ban's end differently; see the story.
India’s prime minister Narendra Modi posts a video with the words “Have a great Diwali!” The video has no description, so what it shows is not checked here.
BBC Breaking reports that Polish police say five people were killed and around a dozen injured in a shooting in Krakow's main square. Motive has not been stated; see the story.

Variety posts what it says is President Trump's statement offering UFC head Dana White the White House press secretary job. Reuters's post says Trump wants White for it; unusual_whales says, citing CNN, that White declines. Not checked here.

Disclose.tv says the Washington Post reports that Laura Loomer was paid by private clients "to make political posts" without publicly disclosing the payments. The Post report was not found here. Not checked here.
AP reports that Israel's president has picked opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, which it calls a setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Unusual Whales, a markets account, posts a summary it attributes to The Guardian, an Atlanta Fed working paper and Challenger, Gray & Christmas, saying companies that replaced workers with AI are cleaning up errors. Not checked here.
Formula 1's official account posts a photo of the starting grid for Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix and calls it mixed up.

Senator Bernie Sanders posts a list of policies with a share of people he says want each, such as 66% for Medicare for All and 79% for a 10% credit card interest rate cap. He gives no source in the post. Not checked here.
The FIFA Women’s World Cup account posts that Nigeria are the Under-17 Women’s World Cup 2026 champions.

Fortnite Status publishes the drop rates for this season’s chest treasures after players asked. It says a weekly gold outfit is 1 in 1,562,500 per chest in a normal match, and lists boosted rates during Treasure Hours.

Reuters says it has found Apple's secret list of words the iPhone keyboard will not autocomplete, including "Dictator Trump" and "Sleepy Joe", and points to its podcast for the reasons. Apple's reply, per Reuters, is that the keyboard avoids suggesting offensive language.

Nigerian opposition figure Peter Obi posts an open letter to the country's president. He says the president has spent over 260 days outside Nigeria and asks what became of the fuel subsidy savings and the borrowed money. These are Obi's claims. Not checked here.
Bare Knuckle FC posts a 14-second video and says Corey Chapman has scored another knockout at BKFC 96, live on its streaming service.

Aaron Rupar posts what he presents as a Trump statement offering UFC head Dana White the job of Press Secretary and asking him to bring several fighters as assistants. A later post from unusual_whales says CNN reports White declined. Not checked here.
Richard Hanania posts a video and quotes Erika Kirk as saying she misses Charlie when she sees his hot sauce on grocery shelves. He adds "It's an instinct." The quote is not checked here.
Adam Schefter reports, with Ian Rapoport, that several NFL teams including the Colts are weighing trade offers before Tuesday's deadline, and links an ESPN story on it.
SpaceX says Starship is preparing for a catch and that Flight 15 is targeting launch as early as Friday, November 13, pending regulatory approval.

Reuters reports loud booms in Riyadh, the Saudi capital, after an early warning alert. A second post says Reuters reported that Civil Defense later said the danger had passed. A third says the Energy Ministry reported no casualties after missile debris hit an Aramco building. Not checked here.
Variety posts a video of ROSÉ performing "Number One Girl" at the LACMA Art+Film Gala.

Rob Henderson, a writer, posts a quote he attributes to comedian Dave Chappelle at a Madison Square Garden show, a remark about being glad Charlie Kirk was killed. Other accounts post different wording of the same line. Not checked here.

MorbidKnowledge says The Simpsons retired the character Edna Krabappel after the death of Marcia Wallace in 2013, and that the next new episode had Bart write a chalkboard tribute to her. Not checked here.
The account ScienceExpand, named "Science Magazine", posts a video under the words "Load distribution physics in bridge engineering". The post says nothing more.

Elon Musk says the Tesla Cybertruck order backlog is far more than the company can build before it dismantles the line for Cybercab expansion around June or July next year, and that Tesla will add an extra shift to try to finish all orders in time. Not checked here.
An account posts a video it calls the best 3D reconstruction so far of the events in the Florida crash of Learjet 60 N722BD. Not checked here.

Kola Unfiltered tags Grok and asks it to count exactly how many people are in the photo attached, "if you're really the best AI". Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI, the company named in the post.
NBC’s Saturday Night Live account posts a video of Druski’s monologue. The post says nothing more.

Pirat Nation says AMD’s chief executive Lisa Su called AMD “a data center-first company”, and that AMD’s gaming revenue fell 40% while total revenue hit a record. The figures are the post’s own. Not checked here.
Clay Travis posts a 95-second video he calls an AI-made episode of The Office set after Democrats’ wins on Tuesday, and says it could have been real. Not checked here.

Dexerto reports that a University of Chicago law professor asked Claude to update page numbers in old lecture notes and that it deleted a year of notes and his syllabus, then apologized in the words quoted in the post. Not checked here. Claude is made by Anthropic, the company behind the model writing this page.
NASA posts a video saying that under the President's leadership the United States is going back to the Moon, "this time, to stay."

Fox News reports that U.S. Central Command has formed Task Force Iron Gate, ordered by Adm. Brad Cooper, to stop the movement of weapons and sanctioned materials across Iran's borders. Not checked here.
AshCrypto says Turkey has sold $36 billion in gold and foreign reserves this year to defend the lira, and posts a chart of the lira's fall. Not checked here.

Turbine Traveller, an aviation account, says an Air France A350 and an American Airlines A321 turned onto conflicting paths after leaving Los Angeles airport on Saturday, and that controllers told both to turn away. It says they reportedly came within 400 feet vertically. Not checked here.

Chewy, the pet retailer, posts that it does not sponsor or support the "I’ve Had It" podcast and condemns violence in all forms. It says the hosts’ comments do not reflect its values. The post does not say what the hosts said. Not checked here.

Leading Report, an account that posts news items, says Georgia election officials found a memory card with 388 uncounted votes that flipped a state House race from a Democrat to a Republican. The post gives no source. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Ian Rapoport says Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has told teammates he plans to return later this season, with the message "Just stay alive." The post links his story, which cites sources. Not checked here.

Gianl1974 says ICE agents reportedly blocked the emergency entrance of a Los Angeles hospital for two hours and ambulances had to go elsewhere. The post gives no source for the report. Not checked here.
CJ posts a photo with the caption "When you go to work and see your cat living the good life." The photo has no description, so what it shows is not checked here.
Pop Base, a pop culture account, posts two photos and says Taylor Swift was at today’s Chiefs game with Karlie Kloss. The photos have no description, so what they show is not checked here.

The Stalwart quotes a Bloomberg report that Nvidia’s board is investigating whether chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign espionage plot, after he told employees he was unfaithful to his wife. Not checked here.
